column1: # Inclusion rule: the company itself tied the workforce action to AI. No analyst speculation.
# Attribution: explicit | partial | capacity. Sources linked per row. https://revolutio.si/layoffs/

column7: what_they_said
CTO (Sep 10): AI push has "freed capacity equivalent to 20,000 workers"; the subsequent September-quarter results showed headcount down 243,044 → 236,328.
column10: Large-deal bookings fell 59% the same quarter — demand weakness is doing real work here too.

column7: 8-K discloses a reduction "primarily within Product and Technology"; the filing does not name AI.
column10: Second round of 2026; media tied it to the AI strategy, the filing itself does not.

column7: Official blog announces cuts "as we focus our people, investments, and energy" on the AI-first transformation.
column10: Follows ~15,000 cuts in 2025 that the company framed as org changes, not AI.

column7: Annual 10-K discloses a 13% workforce decline over fiscal 2026, citing AI deployment; savings feed the data-center buildout.
column10: The clearest "payroll dollars → GPU clusters" case on record.

column7: CEO email: layoffs "sharpen focus" on big bets "including infusing AI" across the company.
CEO letter: "This is a new way of working, and we need to leverage AI across every facet of our jobs."
CFO on earnings call: streamlining plus "step up" of AI and automation toward $1.5B in savings.
column10: Company did not confirm the reported scale; plan, not a single event.

column7: CFO framed the cuts against record AI capex; company language stays performance-based.
column10: A later Reuters investigation documented an explicit AI-replacement plan behind the performance framing.

column7: Cuts attributed "in part" to a shift toward AI and automation.
Dorsey: "A significantly smaller team, using the tools we’re building, can do more and do it better."
The layoff memo itself does not mention AI; months earlier Jassy said agents mean "fewer people doing some of the jobs that are being done today."
column10: Included on the strength of Jassy’s public framing, not the memo — the gap between the two is itself the signal.

column7: Cuts framed as redirecting resources toward expanding AI systems and capabilities.
Blames the "new realities of AI" for cutting nearly half the company.
Benioff on the cut: "I need less heads" — support workload moved to AI agents.
Company cited org changes; Reuters framed the cuts "amid hefty investments in artificial intelligence."
column10: Followed a 6,000/3% round in May 2025 with the same framing.

column7: Cuts announced as AI tools shake up the ed-tech category it once led.
"Network of the Future" automation and AI-driven efficiency named alongside Amazon volume pullback and tariffs.
column10: AI/automation is one of several stated drivers — the Amazon glide-down is the primary one.

column7: CEO email: cuts needed to "prioritize investment in critical areas like AI."
AI assistant "doing the equivalent work of 700 full-time [customer service] agents."
column10: Not a layoff announcement — contractor headcount, not employees. In May 2025 the CEO said they cut "too deep" and began re-hiring humans.

column7: 8-K CEO email: reorganizing to reallocate "substantial" investment toward AI-driven products.
column10: The same email says over 1,000 of the 1,800 were performance exits — the AI framing and the mechanics diverge.

column7: €2B company-wide transformation program focused "entirely" on AI capabilities.
column10: Restructuring, not pure layoffs — company said most affected roles move to retraining or are backfilled, with headcount roughly flat by end-2025.

column7: CEO memo cites "the era of AI" and slowing growth; investments redirected to AI.
CEO: hiring paused for roles AI could do — "I could easily see 30% of these roles replaced by AI in five years."
column10: Attrition without backfill, not a layoff announcement — the quietest form of AI workforce change.
